punchline: Washington trailed at halfway in Berlin, then rowed as one and beat Italy by 0.6 seconds.
thirty_sec: In the 1936 Berlin final, a University of Washington crew of working-class young men drew lane six, barely heard the start and trailed at halfway. Their stroke was ill, their coxswain called for a higher rate, and the boat came through to beat Italy by 0.6 seconds. Daniel James Brown tells it in The Boys in the Boat.
key_contrast: Matching the rhythm, not pulling harder
